newsitem.title: UK: McAlpine new leader of UK Referendum Movement.
newsitem.headline: McAlpine new leader of UK Referendum Movement.

text.p: Lord Robert McAlpine will succeed Sir James Goldsmith, who died on Friday after battling cancer, as leader of the Referendum Movement, a spokesman said on Sunday.

A former treasurer and deputy chairman of the Conservative Party, McAlpine joined Goldsmith's Referendum Party in 1996. He was chairman of both the party and the movement that evolved from it after Britain's election in May 1.

Although the Referendum Party, which campaigned against further European Union integration, won 800,000 votes it failed to secure a seat in the election which resulted in a landslide Labour Party win.
The movement plans to continue to campaign for a referendum on further integration with Europe.
A spokesman said McAlpine will be calling a meeting soon to decide how the movement will proceed following Goldsmith's death.
The 64-year-old billionaire died from a heart attack after a recurrence of pancreatic cancer that was first diagonosed in 1985.
